name: Refugee Status (UNHCR Mandate Determination)

requirements.blocker_text: Algeria has no domestic asylum law or national refugee-status-determination body -- UNHCR itself conducts refugee status determination directly under its own mandate. Process: contact UNHCR by email with personal details; a registration interview (biographic data, photograph, iris scan, fingerprints) resulting in an asylum-seeker certificate to be carried at all times; a formal status-determination interview on the applicant's fear of return; a decision (a refugee card on recognition, or a written explanation on rejection); and a 30-day window to appeal a rejection in writing. The process takes several months, with no fixed statutory deadline. Free interpretation is provided for languages other than English, French, or Arabic. UNHCR may close a file if the applicant misses the initial interview without contact for 3 weeks, misses two determination interviews without valid reason, or fails to attend a notification appointment within 30 days.
requirements.fix_path: Contact UNHCR Algeria by email to register and complete the interview and status-determination process.

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (refugee card), though not tied to any Algerian government residence status

sources.title: UNHCR Help Algeria -- confirms UNHCR (not the Algerian government) directly determines refugee status, full procedural steps, timelines, appeal window, file-closure conditions

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Algeria). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to UNHCR's own country help page, tier 2 (not a government source, and cannot be, since this is precisely the point of the finding below). GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE, MARQUEE STRUCTURAL FINDING: Algeria is the FIRST country built in this entire dataset with NO domestic asylum law and NO national government body deciding refugee status at all -- UNHCR conducts mandate-based refugee status determination directly, entirely outside Algeria's own legal/administrative system. This has real, disclosed consequences modeled conservatively in the outcome fields: a UNHCR refugee card is not itself an Algerian residence permit, and work_rights, study_rights, and family_can_join are set to the most restrictive defaults ('none'/'restricted'/false) since no source reviewed confirmed that UNHCR-mandate refugee recognition converts into any actual Algerian legal status, work authorization, or path to residence, naturalization, or citizenship -- a stark contrast with this dataset's other asylum files (Guatemala, DR Congo, Venezuela, Slovenia), where national law defines concrete rights attached to recognition. This gap itself is the most important thing this file communicates, more than any specific procedural timeline.
